title: build-v2 checkpoint
description: What one run carries between its phase commands: `<run_dir>/checkpoint.json`, announced in `<run_dir>/checkpoint.log` the same way the receipt is. Each phase reads it, adds its own facts, and writes it whole. Nothing is re-derived from a conversation: the contract comes from the build doc at `contract`, the source set and the identity from git and the component at `preflight`, the answer from the file at `record-answer`, and `report` uses exactly those. `records_pin` is the head the run's state was read against; `report` compares the log with it BEFORE its own levelling pass, so an event another writer appended between two phases is a named conflict rather than something this run silently builds on.

phase.description: the last phase that completed. A phase command against the wrong phase is a usage slip (exit 2), and a command on a run that already ended reports the recorded outcome and writes nothing.

input_sha256.description: the canonical serialization of the validated input, so a later phase cannot be pointed at another run

input.description: the validated input, as `references/input.schema.json` describes it

at.description: the RFC 3339 UTC instant the run started; the card event carries it

contract.description: the slice as the document states it (the `contract` block of the result)

source_set.description: the three lists and the base (the `source_set` block of the result)

identity.description: the six-field identity as `records.py identity` computed it

card_before.description: the slice's card as preflight read it

records.description: what preflight read from the component (the `records` block of the result, before the append)

answer.description: the recorded executor answer, as `references/answer.schema.json` describes it

terminal.description: set once a phase command delivered a terminal status; every later phase command returns this and writes nothing

writes.description: every file the run has written so far, in write order

decision.description: the facts the card decision was made on, written before the transaction opens: the out-of-scope list, the check rows, and the card before and after. A pass that settles an unfinished transaction re-delivers these rather than recomputing them, because a rerun check could observe something else and the decision being settled was made on what is here.
